course_description:
This course provides students with the opportunity to learn about Indigenous Australian peoples and their music making; examine the diverse forms of Indigenous performance; and explore how Indigenous Australian performers simultaneously resist and use colonialist constructions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander performance to create new and exciting forms. Please note that this course offering may be cancelled if fewer than 10 students enrol.

This course provides students with the opportunity to learn about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and their music making; examine the diverse forms of Indigenous performance; and explore how Indigenous performers simultaneously resist and use colonialist constructions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander performance to create new and exciting forms.

course_aims: The course aims to deconstruct categories of Indigenous Australian performance such as traditional and contemporary; situate Indigenous Australian performers in terms of their fluid and dynamic identities; relate performance practice to identity, authority, ownership, power and knowledge; understand the complex relationship between performance and country; and, re/presentations of Indigenous Australian performance. In this course you will ultimately increase your understanding of the impact of colonialism on Indigenous Australian peoples and their contemporary music making; raise your awareness of the diversity of Indigenous performance; and examine how Indigenous Australian performers simultaneously resist and use colonialist constructions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander performance to create new and exciting forms.

learning_outcomes.description: Interpret, critically analyse and reflect upon discourse about Indigenous Australian performers with reference to social, historical, and political contexts.
Relate Indigenous Australian performance practices to broader social, historical and political contexts.
Demonstrate a knowledge of issues underpinning Indigenous Australian performance.
Understand the impact of colonialism on the experiences of Indigenous performers historically and in contemporary contexts, and consider your own positioning in relation to this.
Demonstrate an ability to undertake independent research relating to Indigenous performance and share the results of that research with peers.

assessment_details.title: In class written reflection
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Each student submits a one-page reflection during weeks 4, 5, 7, 8 and 11. These reflections are hand-written at the end of class and then handed in. They are to be 1x A4 page maximum. These reflections should address a topic discussed during in-class discussions that week and include 1) a brief summary of the relevant issue brought up during in-class discussion, and 2) your personal reflection on the issue in terms of your own experiences of Indigenous music making and how it speaks to one or more academic readings you have completed for the course so far. Each reflection is marked out of 10, but only the best three (3) reflections will be counted (for a maximum of 30 points). Active participation during in-class discussions will be important to these reflections. Marking criteria and marking rubrics are available in the ‘Assessment’ folder in Blackboard for this course. The reflections are handed in during class in hardcopy (see Learning Activities for the schedule and Blackboard for further details). You must submit your assignment by the due time, on the due date. You will hand in all work for that week’s assessment at the end of the class for the relevant week.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Note that 5 reflections are made available with only the best 3 contributing to a student's final grade. This means a student can miss two reflections and still achieve the maximum possible marks for the In-class Written Reflection assessment component of the course (30%)

assessment_details.title: Digital Story
assessment_details.task_description: Length: 10 minutes maximum This is a group activity (4 students per group). You are required to create a digital story. The digital story will include the following: An aspect of Indigenous music making which interests your group and has become the core concept in this course for your group Thoughts about Indigenous music - these can be written, video-based, song excerpts, images Reference to literature about Indigenous music Reference to perspectives of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander musicians Reference to at least 4 songs discussed in lectures A reference list must be submitted with the digital story. assessment_details.title: Project write-up
assessment_details.task_description: The final piece of assessment for this course is a project write up of the understandings you have gained and gathered from your independent research project. This piece of assessment comprises 40% of your overall mark for this course and should be approximately 3000 words. You are required to reflect on your learning within the final write up. This assessment has a hurdle in which students respond to a question prompt in relation to the essay that is not known in advance, followed by 1-2 follow-up questions in week 12 or 13. Students must pass this oral test to pass the course. If the marker is satisfied that the oral test demonstrates the skills and learning outcomes linked to the essay to a tolerable standard, students will pass the test and the original essay grade stands. You will be guidance throughout the semester on how to complete this task. Your Final Project Write Up should include the following: A detailed description of your project including aims, purpose and approach Analysis of relevant texts and resources to support project Links to materials discussed in class Consideration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives Critical reflection on your personal positioning in relation to your topic and the course weekly topics Consideration of feedback from research proposal Bibliography Read full task description Hide full task description
